scenes.line1: Why do indexes matter in SQL?
scenes.say: Think indexes always make queries faster? Let's see how they really work—and where they trip you up.

scenes.label: B-tree
scenes.say: Most indexes use B-tree structure. It makes finding and sorting data much faster.

right.title: Covering
items: No need to read the table

scenes.say: Composite indexes span several columns. Put the most-used columns first. A covering index holds every column your query needs, so the database skips the table.

scenes.code:
CREATE INDEX idx_emp_dept_salary
ON employees(department_id, salary);
scenes.say: Here's how you make a composite index on department and salary. The order here affects performance.

scenes.question: When do indexes hurt performance?
scenes.right: On columns with many updates or few unique values
scenes.say: Too many indexes slow down writes. Especially avoid them on columns that change a lot, or have only a few unique values.
